authorities.name: Employment Agency (Agentur für Arbeit)
authorities.does: Pays unemployment benefit I (Arbeitslosengeld I) and helps with job search, career advice and training. This is where you register as job-seeking and unemployed.
authorities.doesNot: No Bürgergeld – that is the Jobcenter. No child benefit – that is the Familienkasse.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permit if you have one
Social insurance card or pension insurance number
Notice of termination or fixed-term employment contract
Employer's work certificate (Arbeitsbescheinigung, can be handed in later)
CV and certificates
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Bring a companion or an interpreter
Register as job-seeking up to 3 months before your job ends
Hand in documents later – still register immediately
Ask for a written decision and object within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your local employment agency is the one for your place of residence. The Federal Employment Agency has an official office finder by postcode. You can also register as unemployed online at arbeitsagentur.de.

authorities.name: Immigration Office (Ausländerbehörde)
authorities.does: Issues and extends residence permits, work permits and provisional certificates (Fiktionsbescheinigung). Responsible for all questions about your stay in Germany.
authorities.doesNot: No address registration – that is the Bürgeramt. No asylum procedure – that is the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF).
bring: Passport and current residence permit or visa
Biometric passport photo
Registration certificate or rental contract
Proof of income or employment contract
Proof of health insurance
All letters from the office about your case
rights: Bring a companion or an interpreter
Apply for an extension before your permit expires – it then stays valid until a decision is made
Ask for a certificate that your application was received (Fiktionsbescheinigung)
Ask for a written decision with reasons
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your immigration office is the one of your city or district. Search for “Ausländerbehörde” and the name of your city. The BAMF has an official finder for offices and counselling centres.

authorities.name: BAföG Office
authorities.does: Pays BAföG student and pupil grants. Officially called Amt für Ausbildungsförderung.
authorities.doesNot: No Aufstiegs-BAföG for master craftsman or technician training – apply at your federal state's funding office. No housing benefit – that is the Wohngeldstelle.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permit if you have one
Enrolment certificate or school certificate
Proof of your parents' income (tax assessment from two years ago)
Rental contract or registration certificate
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Apply immediately and hand in documents later – BAföG is only paid from the month of application
Ask for an advance payment if processing takes long
Free advice from the office
Ask for a written decision and object within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: For university students the BAföG office is at the Studierendenwerk of your university. For pupils it is the Amt für Ausbildungsförderung of your city or district. Search for “BAföG” and the name of your university or city.

authorities.name: Citizens' Office (Bürgeramt)
authorities.does: Registers your address and issues ID cards, passports, registration certificates and certificates of conduct. Also called Bürgerbüro or Einwohnermeldeamt depending on the town.
authorities.doesNot: No residence permit – that is the Ausländerbehörde. No housing benefit – that is the Wohngeldstelle.
bring: ID card or passport
Landlord's confirmation of move-in (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, for registration)
Birth or marriage certificate if you are new to Germany
Biometric passport photo (for ID card or passport)
rights: Bring a companion or an interpreter
Register your address within 14 days of moving in – without an appointment if none is available
Take a registration certificate with you straight away
Ask for a short-notice appointment in urgent cases
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your citizens' office is the one of your city or municipality. Search for “Bürgeramt” or “Bürgerbüro” and the name of your city. Appointments are usually booked online. The public services number 115 can help in many regions.

authorities.name: Parental Allowance Office (Elterngeldstelle)
authorities.does: Pays parental allowance (Elterngeld, ElterngeldPlus) and the partnership bonus after a birth. Depending on the federal state it belongs to the city, the district or a state office.
authorities.doesNot: No child benefit – that is the Familienkasse. No maternity pay – that is your health insurance fund.
bring: Child's birth certificate (copy for parental allowance)
ID card or passport of both parents, plus residence permit if you have one
Proof of income for the 12 months before the birth
Health insurance certificate about maternity pay
Employer's confirmation of parental leave
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Apply within 3 months of the birth – it is only paid back for 3 months
Hand in the application immediately and add documents later
Ask for advice before applying
Ask for a written decision and object within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: Search for “Elterngeldstelle” and the name of your city or district. In many federal states you can apply online via ElterngeldDigital – it shows you the office responsible for you.

authorities.name: Family Benefits Office (Familienkasse)
authorities.does: Pays child benefit (Kindergeld) and the child supplement (Kinderzuschlag). Part of the Federal Employment Agency.
authorities.doesNot: No parental allowance – that is the Elterngeldstelle. No Bürgergeld – that is the Jobcenter.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permit if you have one
Tax ID of you and the child
Child's birth certificate
Registration certificate
The last letter from the Familienkasse
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Bring a companion or an interpreter
Hand in documents later – still submit the application immediately
Ask for a confirmation of receipt
Receive child benefit for up to 6 months back
authorities.howToFindLocal: The Familienkasse responsible for you depends on where you live. The Federal Employment Agency has an official office finder by postcode. You can also apply online.

authorities.name: Tax Office (Finanzamt)
authorities.does: Processes your tax return and tax assessments, tax class and allowances. Issues the tax number for self-employed people.
authorities.doesNot: No child benefit – that is the Familienkasse. No tax ID – that is issued by the Federal Central Tax Office.
bring: ID card or passport
Tax ID
Employer's wage tax certificate (Lohnsteuerbescheinigung)
Receipts for expenses (commuting, insurance, childcare)
The last tax assessment
rights: File your tax return online for free via ELSTER
Apply for an extension if you need more time
Object to a tax assessment within one month
Ask for free information about your case
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your tax office is the one for your place of residence. The Federal Central Tax Office has an official tax office finder by postcode.

authorities.name: Jobcenter
authorities.does: Pays Bürgergeld and covers rent and heating if your income is not enough. Supports you with job search and training.
authorities.doesNot: No unemployment benefit I – that is the Agentur für Arbeit. No basic income support in old age – that is the Sozialamt.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permits, of everyone in your household
Rental contract and last utility bill
Bank statements of the last 3 months
Proof of income (pay slips, benefit decisions)
Proof of assets (savings, insurance policies)
Health insurance card
rights: Bring a companion or an interpreter
Submit the application immediately – Bürgergeld is paid from the first day of the application month, add documents later
Ask for a confirmation of receipt
Object to a decision within one month
Ask for an advance if you have run out of money
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your Jobcenter is the one for your place of residence. The Federal Employment Agency has an official office finder by postcode. The hotline covers Jobcenters run jointly with the employment agency – municipal Jobcenters have their own numbers.

authorities.name: Youth Welfare Office (Jugendamt)
authorities.does: Pays advance maintenance (Unterhaltsvorschuss) for single parents and helps with childcare places, paternity, custody and contact. Advises families on separation and parenting.
authorities.doesNot: No child benefit – that is the Familienkasse. No parental allowance – that is the Elterngeldstelle.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permit if you have one
Child's birth certificate
Proof about maintenance (court order, payments or letters from the other parent)
Registration certificate
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Free advice, even without an application
Bring a companion or an interpreter
Ask for legal assistance (Beistandschaft) so the office enforces maintenance for you
Ask for a written decision and object within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your youth welfare office is the one of your city or district. Search for “Jugendamt” and the name of your city.

authorities.name: Health Insurance Fund (Krankenkasse)
authorities.does: Pays sick pay, maternity pay and cures or rehabilitation and co-insures family members for free. Exempts you from co-payments if your income is low.
authorities.doesNot: No care allowance – that is the Pflegekasse at your health insurance fund. No reduced earning capacity pension – that is the pension insurance.
bring: Health insurance card
Doctor's sick note
Proof of income (for family insurance or co-payment exemption)
Maternity record book (for maternity pay)
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Choose your health insurance fund freely and switch
Object to a refusal within one month
Ask for written reasons if a benefit is refused
Ask a bank for a basic account if you do not have one
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your health insurance fund is printed on your insurance card – the phone number is there too. Every fund has branches in larger cities.

authorities.name: Long-term Care Insurance Fund (Pflegekasse)
authorities.does: Determines the care level and pays care allowance, care services, respite care and care aids. It is located at your health insurance fund.
authorities.doesNot: No sick pay – that is the Krankenkasse. If the money for care is not enough, the Sozialamt helps with Hilfe zur Pflege.
bring: Insurance card of the person needing care
Medical reports and medication plan
Care diary: what help the person needs every day
Power of attorney if you apply for someone else
IBAN of the account payments should go to
rights: Apply informally by phone – payments start from that day
Have a trusted person with you at the assessment
Ask for free care counselling
Object to the care level within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: The Pflegekasse is at the health insurance fund of the person needing care – the number is on the insurance card. Search for the name of the health insurance fund and “Pflegekasse”.

authorities.name: Pension Insurance (Rentenversicherung)
authorities.does: Pays old-age pension, reduced earning capacity pension and survivors' pension and funds rehabilitation. Provides pension information and clarifies your insurance record.
authorities.doesNot: No basic income support in old age if the pension is not enough – that is the Sozialamt. No sick pay – that is the Krankenkasse.
bring: ID card or passport
Pension insurance number or social insurance card
Insurance record or last pension information letter
Proof of training, child-raising periods and work abroad
Medical reports (for reduced earning capacity or rehabilitation)
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Free advice and help filling in the application
Bring a companion or an interpreter
Apply for your pension 3 months before it should start
Object to a decision within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: The German Pension Insurance has advice centres in all larger cities. On the official website you can find and book an appointment near you. The free hotline is nationwide.

authorities.name: Social Welfare Office (Sozialamt)
authorities.does: Pays basic income support in old age and for reduced earning capacity, subsistence support and help with care costs. Covers funeral costs if nobody can pay them.
authorities.doesNot: No Bürgergeld for people who are able to work – that is the Jobcenter. No housing benefit – that is the Wohngeldstelle.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permit if you have one
Pension decision or decision on reduced earning capacity
Rental contract and utility bill
Bank statements of the last 3 months
Proof of assets and insurance policies
Health insurance card
rights: Apply immediately – payments start from the day the office learns of your need
Bring a companion or an interpreter
Ask for a confirmation of receipt
Object to a decision within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your social welfare office is the one of your city or district. Search for “Sozialamt” and the name of your city. You can also apply for basic income support in old age at the pension insurance – it forwards the application.

authorities.name: Pension and Welfare Office (Versorgungsamt)
authorities.does: Determines the degree of disability and issues the severely disabled person's pass with its markers. Also responsible for compensation after violent crimes (social compensation).
authorities.doesNot: No care level – that is the Pflegekasse. No reduced earning capacity pension – that is the pension insurance.
bring: ID card or passport
Medical reports, findings and hospital discharge letters
Names and addresses of your doctors
Passport photo (for the pass)
Previous decision if you are reporting a deterioration
rights: Apply without seeing a doctor first – the office asks the doctors itself
Bring a companion or an interpreter
Ask to see your file if the application is refused
Object to the determined degree within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: The office has different names depending on the federal state: Versorgungsamt, Amt für Soziales, Landesamt or the district. Search for “Schwerbehindertenausweis beantragen” and the name of your federal state or district.

authorities.name: Housing Benefit Office (Wohngeldstelle)
authorities.does: Pays housing benefit (Wohngeld) as a subsidy towards rent or the costs of your own home if your income is low. Part of the city or district administration.
authorities.doesNot: No housing benefit if you receive Bürgergeld or basic income support – rent is already included there. No Bürgergeld – that is the Jobcenter.
bring: ID card or passport, plus residence permits, of everyone in your household
Rental contract and proof of rent payments
Proof of income of everyone in your household
Registration certificate
IBAN of your bank account
rights: Apply immediately – housing benefit is paid from the month of application, add documents later
Ask for a confirmation of receipt
Bring a companion or an interpreter
Object to a decision within one month
authorities.howToFindLocal: Your housing benefit office is the one of your city or municipality, in smaller places the district. Search for “Wohngeldstelle” and the name of your city. Many federal states offer an online application.
